appraisal_events.evidence: Bloch fails to notice how cool and unenthusiastic Saint-Loup's invitation actually was, and instead presses the narrator repeatedly to fix a day to go to Doncières, an insistence the narrator says was pushed 'à un point dont on était agacé,' risking the 'ridicule' of rushing to accept.
appraisal_events.explanation: The narrator portrays Bloch as socially obtuse and overeager, oblivious to the real coolness behind Saint-Loup's invitation and pressing it to an annoying, faintly ridiculous degree.

status_effects.explanation: Bloch's excessive insistence and failure to perceive Saint-Loup's real reluctance make him appear socially maladroit, though the narrator notes his faults are offset by real qualities, keeping the diminishment moderate.
